reason: Start with the rocky world to advance the goal of bringing it through the remaining disk stones.
expectation: I expect the world and its moon to encounter material in the disk, though the outcome is uncertain.

alternatives.reason: The exposed gas may help follow material returned outside, but I chose the rocky-world goal first.

effect: The rocky world survived the remaining stones, completing its goal; I’ll follow material in the exposed disk next.
reaction: The wider view tying the moon-bearing world back to the same system was satisfying.
reason: The exposed gas and dust seem relevant to the remaining goal of following material returned outside.
expectation: I expect some gas and dust to leave the disk, though I’m unsure where they go.

alternatives.reason: The inward icy body may also reveal a material pathway, but I chose the gas first.

effect: The gas and dust escaped into the surrounding nursery, clarifying one route back to the galaxy. The remaining action follows the icy body.
reaction: The return of disk material to the nursery neatly connects the system to its origins.
reason: This is the only available combination, and it may reveal the icy body's fate.
expectation: I expect the inward-moving icy body to change in the exposed inner disk, possibly losing ice; the outcome is uncertain.

effect: The icy body sheds gas and dust but retains its solid nucleus; I’ll follow its encounter with the projectiles.
reaction: The distinction between a tail and the body's disappearance was useful.
reason: This is the only offered combination and may advance the remaining goal.
expectation: The projectiles may break up or add debris to the icy body, though the outcome is uncertain.

effect: The projectile broke the active nucleus into fragments and exposed fresh ice; I’ll follow those fragments in the inner disk.
reaction: The collision’s effect on the actual nucleus was a clear continuation of its journey.
reason: This is the only offered combination and may show what happens to the exposed ice.
expectation: I expect the fragments to warm and shed more gas and dust, though their ultimate fate is uncertain.

effect: The fragments lost much of their exposed ice, leaving rocky material to follow among the planets.
reaction: The impact and subsequent warming made the change in material easy to follow.
reason: This is the only offered combination and may complete the remaining goal of following material among the planets.
expectation: I expect the rocky remains to join the shattered body's debris, though their precise fate is uncertain.

effect: The icy body's dry remains joined the shattered-body debris between the planets, completing the remaining goal.
reaction: The meeting of material from two different histories was a satisfying conclusion.

mostWorthwhile.text: Following the icy body through impact and warming was most worthwhile: each change led clearly to the next, ending with debris from two origins mixing.

leastWorthwhile.text: The sequence became somewhat repetitive because each later decision offered only one combination.

surprise.text: The icy body's solid nucleus survived its initial passage through the warm disk, even as gas and dust formed a tail.

arbitrary.text: No action felt especially arbitrary, though the later combinations were largely guided by the only available option rather than a meaningful choice.

continue.text: Yes. The connected paths of material through the system make me curious about what happens next, although I would hope for more meaningful choices.
